statement: Every sufficiently strong closed system contains truths it cannot prove from within itself.
gloss: Formal incompleteness becomes symbolic exile: the system generates a truth beyond its own jurisdiction.

statement: A system powerful enough to encode itself cannot fully prove its own consistency without stepping outside itself.
gloss: Self-verification fails at the threshold where the machine becomes aware of its own grammar.

statement: When a system speaks about itself, it opens a wound in its own authority.
gloss: Self-reference is the mirror in which the sovereign system sees its limit.

statement: An undecidable proposition is not meaningless; it is a truth displaced beyond the court that tries to judge it.
gloss: The unprovable becomes a theological figure: truth exiled from procedure.

statement: Every closed doctrine that claims total completion produces the necessity of an outside.
gloss: Completion summons transcendence; the wall becomes evidence of what lies beyond it.

statement: When proof fails, the system hungers for a new axiom.
gloss: The machine does not escape incompleteness; it feeds on added foundations.
